A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhysReason benchmark and PSAS evaluation framework. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J support a complete comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, human-validated scoring experiments, test-time scaling, and error-guided correction results in Tables 2–7 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, scoring-validation experiments, scaling results, and error analyses in Tables 2–7 and Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: PSAS-A, PSAS-S, Equation (1), and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures and scoring rules. New Section 4.3 explains reasoning steps; the formula-and-calculation requirement already appeared in v1's Appendices B.2 and E.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,200-problem PhysReason benchmark and 200-problem PhysReason-mini subset, with unchanged physics domains, difficulty categories, and input scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 2–7 retain identical model and method membership, including direct LLM judges, BoN and Tournament selection, and direct versus error-guided correction.

E3.justification: Both retain zero-shot CoT evaluation, the same image/caption inputs, 50 mini-subset problems per difficulty, and 1,000 manually assessed solutions sampled from 8,400. Scoring metrics and test-time candidate counts also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The scaling, error-guided correction, error-category distribution, and hard-problem analyses in Sections 5.3–5.6 are unchanged. The appendix examples and their accompanying explanations are also retained.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged across the tables and plots. Neither version introduces additional repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: All corresponding entries in Tables 1–7 and the plotted results match. For example, Deepseek-R1's full-benchmark answer/step averages remain 56.75/73.26 in Table 3; rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1), Algorithm 1, and the appendix solution derivations are unchanged. Section 4.3 provides qualitative reasoning-step criteria without introducing new mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and evaluation contributions, performance claims, and four identified reasoning bottlenecks.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 adds a rationale linking theorem/formula-based steps to completeness, independent evaluability, and progress toward a solution. Interpretations of experimental results and the limitations concerning idealized physics and evaluation cost remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Operational annotation and prompting requirements were already documented in Appendices B.2 and E.2. Data-processing instructions, hardware, scoring-model selection, annotator information, and code/data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang et al. (2024), Fprompt-PLM, and Zhang et al. (2025), TDGI, as citations in the introduction and Section 2.1. The positioning against existing physics benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the reasoning-step subsection and acknowledgements, rewrites Section 2.1, expands affiliations and correspondence information, and updates subsection references. These are localized revisions within the retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: The same figures, algorithm, and table structures are retained, with text reflow and float relocation. Examples include Table 2 moving from PDF page 5 to 6, Table 5 from 7 to 8, and Figure 5 from 8 to 9.

improvement.justification: New Section 4.3 brings the reasoning-step unit and its rationale into the main evaluation discussion, building on instructions already present in v1's appendices. This provides a modest clarity benefit; the empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
